title: 1871: fire-alarm boxes, hydrants and goods on the walks round the stops
items: Red cast-iron fire-alarm boxes stand at the corners Edwards' 1871 directory lists as the fire telegraph's stations, and hydrants at the corners, the year's new ones where the Board of Public Works set them.

Lake Street's telegraph poles are tall, with eight crossarms strung with wires, as a late-1860s photograph shows them, and fire-alarm wires run from the Court House cupola to the roofs round the square.
Packing cases, barrels, crates and sacks stand on the walks of the wholesale streets; coal-hole plates and cellar doors are let into the walks, and carriage blocks stand before the houses.
Barbers' poles stand at the corners the directory gives five barbers, and a carved Highlander before a cigar store at Dearborn and Madison.
It is Sunday, so no shop's goods for sale are set out, and nothing stands in a doorway, a crossing or the path along the walk.
